scope: Proposition 3.4 (Polarization) of the manuscript “The Kerr–Newman Penrose Inequality for Axisymmetric Electrovacuum Exteriors” (preprints/The-Kerr-Newman-Penrose-Inequality-for-Axisymmetric-Electrovacuum-Exteriors-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ff3098c8faf29685), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The data (g0, k0) extend smoothly through the axis, have the stated asymptotic decay, and have the same ADM energy as (g, K). For every invariant surface, its area and future expansion are unchanged. Let µ0, J0 be the constraint densities of (g0, k0), with J0 a covector. Write dA = fadAh and set s = (−Be, Ee, −Xfa/2). Then 16πµ0 = 2 |DX|2 g0 + |s|2 , 8πJ0 = 2s · DX. (3.9) The source combinations on the right are smooth across the axis. On a signed axis tube s1, s2 are odd of order y, and s3 is even of order y2. In particular the polarized data satisfy the dominant energy condition.
